main_artifacts.name: The Star Fragment
main_artifacts.description: A piece of a fallen star, shattered into nine fragments by the God Toad. Each shard bestows immense, unique power upon its bearer, but also subtly corrupts them to fit a grand, unknown design.
main_artifacts.lore: When the star fell, it illuminated the night sky for seven days. The God Toad, witnessing its descent, knew such power could not remain whole.
main_artifacts.locations: Scattered across the Midlands, held by the Star Bearers

main_artifacts.name: The Fireflower
main_artifacts.description: A legendary artifact that grants mastery over flame. It is said to be hidden in a volcanic dungeon, guarded by a fire dragon and its cult.
main_artifacts.lore: Born from the heart of the first volcano, the Fireflower's petals were scattered by the great eruption that shaped the continents.
main_artifacts.locations: Petals distributed among world leaders and major factions

main_artifacts.name: The Mushroom of Life
main_artifacts.description: A relic with the power to restore life itself. It grows in a cursed, time-distorting forest, protected by ancient guardians who test all who seek it.
main_artifacts.lore: The first life in the world sprouted from this ancient fungus. Its spores carry the essence of creation itself.

star_bearers.name: Rebellion
star_bearers.title: The Dark Sovereign
star_bearers.powers: Rebellion is not a brute; he is a researcher. Rather than simply wielding his shard, he studies it — running a sustained set of "star experiments" to extract the true, undiluted power locked inside a single fragment. His command of the shard is exploratory and clinical, and it is that willingness to experiment on something unstable that makes him genuinely dangerous. He has learned things about the fragments that even the God Toad may not have intended anyone to learn.
star_bearers.fragment_desc: The Crown Shard is the largest and most powerful fragment of the star, containing the core essence of leadership and dominion. In Rebellion's hands it is less a crown than a specimen — something to be studied, dissected, and pushed past its safe limits. It pulses with a black light that seems to absorb rather than emit energy.
star_bearers.history: Rebellion is a Toad — and, more surprisingly, the God Toad's own second-in-command. His name is not a boast but a description: he does not agree with everything the God Toad does. Where the God Toad is coldly pragmatic, Rebellion is curious to the point of recklessness. He became obsessed with a single question — how much power a lone shard truly holds — and began a program of star experiments to find out. That research led him to a realization the God Toad never advertised: the shards fell from the sky, and they are powered by pure anger. They are, in other words, deeply unstable. Rebellion took his findings to a research laboratory in the Regal Empire, buried deep inside a volcano — the site of the events recorded as 'The Star Shard Caves and the Tanuki's Origin.' What became of the shard there, one can guess. Whether it now rests in Fawful's hands remains to be seen.

star_bearers.name: Charismatic
star_bearers.title: The Battle Master
star_bearers.powers: Charismatic fights at maxed-out 9,999 stats with effectively infinite damage and resistance — on paper, an unstoppable ally who makes defeating even the God Toad look like a breeze. His real weapon, however, is misdirection. A master manipulator with slick, laid-back hair and an immaculate tux, his purpose is distraction: he sends the party on wild goose chases that lead nowhere, all while appearing to help. The question the whole encounter turns on is simple and unsettling — can a human really defeat a god, and is he actually trying to?
star_bearers.fragment_desc: The Warrior Shard contains the star's aspect of conflict and triumph, burning with a constant internal fire and granting its bearer flawless combat instinct. On Charismatic — a man who would rather be cutting cloth than throwing punches — it reads less like a gift and more like a leash.
star_bearers.history: Charismatic was never a warrior. He was a famous fashion designer — the one who created Bowser's own tuxedo for his wedding — and he never wanted the shard at all. He wants to make clothes, not fight people. But the moment the fragment chose him, a task was assigned to him, and something now keeps him from simply walking away. He presents himself as Archie's 'best friend,' though Archie does not remember him, and he cheerfully helps himself to joining Disaster Inc., traveling alongside the party and helping them bring down a star bearer with his impossible stats. It looks like a breeze. Or it should. Because he knows his real task, and the true drama of Charismatic is whether he will follow the rules he was given and stay the course — or whether the designer who just wants to make clothes will finally refuse to turn against the party.

star_bearers.name: Beauty
star_bearers.title: The Toxic Enchanter
star_bearers.powers: Beauty's greatest strength is not force but escape. She is a coward by design: when a fight turns dicy she simply runs, and she is extraordinarily good at it. Rather than trade blows, she gathers intelligence, returning to confront the party again and again in different cosplays, testing new approaches each time and learning from every encounter. She is by-the-books to a fault, and she cares deeply about how she looks — she forgoes practical armor because it makes her appear weak, even though she is not. Perhaps this is a bearer whose conflict does not need to be solved with violence at all.
star_bearers.fragment_desc: The Bloom Shard embodies the star's aspect of growth and transformation, pulsing with green energy and accelerating natural processes around its bearer. In Beauty's care it becomes a tool of appearance and evasion as much as attack — botanical traps to cover a retreat, not to hold a line.
star_bearers.history: Beauty is a bird-person and a member of the Iron Legion — aloof, airheaded, and newly promoted to general. She tries her best, she really does, but she is out of her depth and knows it, which is exactly why her instinct is always to survive rather than win. She treats each confrontation with the party as reconnaissance: arrive in a new disguise, gather fresh intel, attempt a new angle, and vanish before it gets dangerous. Underneath the vanity and the flightiness is someone who is not actually weak — only unwilling to be cornered.

star_bearers.name: Refrain
star_bearers.title: The Tempest
star_bearers.powers: Refrain's defining trait is restraint. They hold out, refusing to use their true potential until the very last possible moment — which is at once their greatest strength and their greatest weakness. For most of any confrontation they fight far below their real capability, weighed down by visible guilt; but when the moment finally comes and it looks as though everything is over, they become capable of massive, decisive attacks. The discipline that makes them predictable is the same discipline that makes them, at the end, overwhelming.
star_bearers.fragment_desc: The Tempest Shard embodies the star's aspect of movement and change, shifting between shades of blue and gray and sometimes throwing off small sparks. Held in check by a bearer determined not to use it, it is a storm kept behind a closed door — until the door finally opens.
star_bearers.history: Little is known about Refrain — and that is the point. At some time in the past they did something. Something very bad. Bad enough that they now carry an immense, self-imposed restraint against the party and show unmistakable guilt toward them, yet they will never say what it was. That silence is the thread: uncovering the truth of what Refrain did may be the key that connects every one of the star bearers together. Whatever the secret is, it is not Refrain's alone.

star_bearers.name: Might
star_bearers.title: The Unstoppable
star_bearers.powers: Might uses his shard to raise armies and bend others to his will, commanding forces large enough to stand between the party and any shard they seek. His paradox is his voice: it is high-pitched, babyish, and loud, and he cannot bear to be heard. So he leads in silence, refusing to speak, which makes issuing orders and commands almost impossible. His enormous strength is undercut by a self-imposed muteness born of shame — an unstoppable force terrified of being laughed at.
star_bearers.fragment_desc: The Might Shard embodies the star's aspect of raw physical dominion — strength, endurance, unbreakable presence. It gave Might everything he asked for and nothing he actually needed, reshaping his body while leaving untouched the one thing he most wanted to change.
star_bearers.history: Might is an orc who was bullied his entire life for his babyish, high-pitched voice. When he obtained the shard, he knew exactly what he wanted from it: his muscles swelled, his frame grew huge and bulky, he became physically imposing in every way — and his voice remained exactly the same. Now he has appointed himself the one who must stop the main party from gathering the star shards, raising armies and forcing others to do his bidding. But he stays silent to hide his voice, and silence makes commanding an army a genuine predicament: if his soldiers ever hear him speak, surely they will mock him, and if they mock him, he will lose the army. His whole reign balances on never being heard.

star_bearers.name: Justice
star_bearers.title: The Arbiter
star_bearers.powers: Justice grows stronger with every worthy enemy she kills. Each of her eight tails harbors the soul of a defeated foe — and not ordinary souls, but those taken from individuals of high potential, the sort one might call BOSSES. Every such kill lets her gain a level and, eventually, another tail. She is building toward eight. Once all eight tails are filled, she will deliver her final verdict — and it will not be aimed at the God Toad, but at someone else entirely.
star_bearers.fragment_desc: The Judgment Shard embodies the star's aspect of law, weight, and finality. In Justice's hands it has become an instrument of accumulation — a ledger of souls, each one a step toward a sentence she has spent decades preparing to pass.
star_bearers.history: Justice is a kitsune judge of the Oathbound Judges who believes, sincerely, that the star shards are useful in the right hands — hers. Behind that conviction is decades of quiet, methodical power-gathering and a secret she guards absolutely. Her daughter is dead. She was only five. The child saw what her mother was studying, understood what her mother was doing, and wanted to be a 'superhero' too. She snuck into her mother's laboratory and injected herself with pure power — and it killed her. Everything Justice has done since, every soul sealed in every tail, every level gained, bends toward the verdict she intends to deliver when the eighth tail is finally filled. It is not the God Toad she is coming for.

star_bearers.name: Self Reflection
star_bearers.title: The Oracle
star_bearers.powers: Self Reflection can see possible futures branching from any present moment. He can communicate through dreams and visions over vast distances. His most valuable ability is Memory Walk, which allows him to project himself and others into past events as observers.
star_bearers.fragment_desc: The Vision Shard contains the star's aspect of perception and foresight. It appears as a clear crystal that sometimes shows swirling images of distant places or times.
star_bearers.history: Originally a scholarly toad who documented the forgotten histories of the Midlands, Self Reflection was chosen for his contemplative nature. When he received the Vision Shard, his consciousness expanded beyond linear time. He established a small sanctuary beside the Lake of Mirrors, where the waters sometimes reflect events yet to occur. Though physically the weakest of the fragment bearers, he is perhaps the most important, as his visions guide the others toward the eventual reunification of all fragments.

star_bearers.name: The Unnamed Bearer
star_bearers.title: Unknown
star_bearers.powers: [RECORD SEALED] The nature, powers, and even the existence of this bearer are unconfirmed. Fragments of testimony contradict one another, and no reliable account of an encounter survives. What little exists has been withheld pending corroboration.
star_bearers.fragment_desc: [RECORD SEALED] The fragment associated with this bearer is undocumented. Its element, appearance, and whereabouts remain unverified.
star_bearers.history: [RECORD SEALED] Waluigi has chosen not to speculate here. Some entries in an encyclopedia are more honest as questions than as answers, and this is one of them. The eighth shard is accounted for on no ledger the archive trusts. That is all the record will say.

god_toad.name: The God Toad
god_toad.title: Original Keeper
god_toad.powers: The God Toad exists simultaneously in multiple planes of reality, making him nearly impossible to truly comprehend, let alone defeat. Those who attempt to perceive his true form often find their minds fractured beyond repair. He can manipulate the very fabric of space and time in limited areas, creating pocket dimensions where physical laws bend to his will. There are accounts of him reversing the flow of time to undo events that displease him, though this appears to drain his power significantly. Some scholars believe he is not a single entity but a collective consciousness inhabiting a shared form, explaining his ability to maintain awareness across vast distances.
god_toad.fragment_desc: The Core Shard is unlike the others—it appears as a void rather than a physical object, a tear in reality through which the pure power of the star flows directly into its bearer. This fragment gives the God Toad his omniscience regarding the other fragments and may be the source of his apparent immortality.
god_toad.history: After being betrayed by his adventuring companions who sought to steal the star's power for themselves, the God Toad shattered the star into nine fragments to prevent its misuse. He kept the Core Shard for himself and distributed the others to trusted followers who would become the Toad Guardians. What few know is that he deliberately corrupted each fragment differently, ensuring that their powers would drive their bearers toward specific goals—all part of a grand design that has been unfolding for centuries. His true motivation remains unknown, but ancient texts suggest he seeks to reshape the Midlands into something 'beyond mortal comprehension.'
